claims.text: The stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is governed by an interaction between thermal-expansion mismatch and dislocation-mediated plasticity.
Combined tensile and thermal loading can provide a unified explanation of the alloy's behavior.
The relevant initial material is polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr with varying degrees of cold work and aging.
The proposed experiment applies tensile and thermal-expansion testing from 293 to 1250 K.
The proposed tensile load extends to 500 MPa.
The relevant high-temperature conditions extend to 1250 °C.
Dislocation density and spatial distribution are the structural mediators.
Mismatch-induced thermal stresses interact with dislocation-mediated plasticity to alter stress–strain behavior.
At 1000 K, the treated or combined-loading condition will have 20% higher yield strength than the as-cast baseline.
At 1000 K, the treated or combined-loading condition will have a 15% lower thermal-expansion coefficient than the as-cast baseline.
The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy is the baseline control.
The proposed response boundary is 293–1250 K and 0–500 MPa.
The relationship between thermal-expansion mismatch and dislocation-mediated plasticity is not well understood.
The effects of cold rolling and aging on the alloy's behavior are not fully quantified.
The hypothesis is falsified if yield strength increases by less than 10% or the thermal-expansion coefficient decreases by less than 5% relative to the as-cast baseline at 1000 K.

contradictions.description: The intervention, boundary, and falsification design specify a maximum of 1250 K, whereas the conditions specify up to 1250 °C (approximately 1523 K). These are materially different temperature limits.
